suppress.notes: Transitive dependency of io.quarkus:quarkus-vertx (via Quarkus platform 3.37.4), not a direct dependency. CVE-2026-44891, CVE-2026-55831, and CVE-2026-55833 are in Netty's STOMP (io.netty.handler.codec.stomp) and SPDY (io.netty.handler.codec.spdy) frame decoders. This application never constructs a STOMP or SPDY server/client and does not expose those protocols; it only uses Netty as the HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 transport underlying the Quarkus Vert.x HTTP server. Matched by CPE rather than packageUrl because dependency-check correlates this CVE against every jar sharing the netty:netty CPE (both netty-transport and netty-transport-classes-epoll were observed flagged across different scan runs, depending on which jar the tool picks as the CPE match target). As of the Quarkus 3.37.4 upgrade (Netty 4.1.136.Final) these three no longer match and dependency-check reports the rule as unused; it is kept for one release cycle because the NVD dataset has previously returned different ID sets for this CPE on different runs. Prune it if the next platform upgrade still shows zero matches.

False positive: these CVEs are against "OpenTelemetry-Go", the Go language implementation of OpenTelemetry, not the Java io.opentelemetry.semconv artifact pulled in transitively by Quarkus's OpenTelemetry/Micrometer integration. Dependency-check's CPE matching cross-matches the shared "opentelemetry" product name across ecosystems; this project has no Go dependencies of any kind. The specific CVE IDs returned against this CPE have shifted between scan runs (CVE-2026-29181/CVE-2026-39883 on one run, CVE-2026-39882/CVE-2026-41178 on another) even though the underlying jar version did not change, so all four observed IDs are listed here; revisit and prune to only the IDs the NVD dataset currently returns next time this file is touched.

Transitive dependency of io.quarkus:quarkus-virtual-threads (via Quarkus platform 3.37.4), not a direct dependency. CVE-2026-15075 and CVE-2026-15076 are in Vert.x's Web Client (io.vertx.ext.web.client.WebClient / WebClientSession) redirect and cookie-domain handling. This backend never uses vertx-web-client to make outbound HTTP requests (confirmed: no WebClient/WebClientSession usage anywhere in backend/src); vertx-core and vertx-auth-common here only back the inbound Quarkus HTTP server. Matched by CPE rather than packageUrl because dependency-check correlates this CVE against every jar sharing the eclipse:vert.x CPE (vertx-core and vertx-auth-common were both observed flagged across different scan runs). As of the Quarkus 3.37.4 upgrade these no longer match and the rule is reported as unused; kept for one release cycle for the same dataset-volatility reason as the Netty rule above.

Added 2026-08-02. CVE-2026-56816 is unbounded buffering of HTTP/3 reserved frames in io.netty.handler.codec.http3.Http3FrameCodec, whose decodeFrame trusts the wire-specified payLoadLength. The affected class exists only on Netty's 4.2.x line, in the separate netty-codec-http3 artifact; the NVD record carries a bare versionEndExcluding of 4.2.16 with no lower bound, so it matches every 4.1.x version too. This build resolves no HTTP/3 or QUIC artifact at all (verified with `mvn dependency:list`), and no jar on the resolved tree contains an Http3FrameCodec class (verified by scanning the 4.1.136.Final jars). The vulnerable code path is therefore absent, not merely unreached: Quarkus serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over TCP here. This is not a case of a fix being unavailable — the four genuinely applicable Netty CVEs from the same advisory batch were fixed by upgrading the platform to 3.37.4 (Netty 4.1.136.Final) rather than suppressed. Revisit if this project ever adopts HTTP/3, or if the NVD record gains a lower version bound and stops matching 4.1.x.
